summary.headline: The Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions for Lynbrook Road water main work and prepared extensive wetland comments on the 250 Turnpike Road 40B project.
summary.summary: The Conservation Commission closed the hearing and issued an Order of Conditions with special construction stipulations for the Southborough DPW water main replacement along Lynbrook Road. Members reviewed a detailed draft comment letter to the Zoning Board of Appeals regarding the 250 Turnpike Road 40B housing proposal, focusing on buffer zone protections, retaining walls, and wildlife crossing designs. The commission also decided against recommending town acquisition for a 1.5-acre parcel on Northborough Road and previewed upcoming land use regulations for town conservation properties.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The commission approved the meeting minutes from March 12, 2026, and adjourned at the conclusion of business.
key_details: Approved minutes of March 12, 2026.
Meeting adjourned at 45:06.

topics.title: Lynbrook Road water main replacement Notice of Intent
topics.summary: The commission reviewed revised engineering plans submitted by consultant Seaver Anderson on behalf of the Southborough Department of Public Works for replacing the water main within the Lynbrook Road right-of-way. Revisions clarified buffer zones, confirmed riverfront areas do not encroach into the work site, adjusted match lines, and substituted straw bales for hay bales in dewatering details. The commission closed the public hearing and voted to issue an Order of Conditions with requirements for contractor pre-construction plan submittals and dewatering reviews.
key_details: Project located in the Lynbrook Road right-of-way near Lovers Lane.
Revised plans stamped and dated March 30, 2026.
Special conditions require final design plans and dewatering setups to be reviewed and approved prior to work.
Public hearing closed and Order of Conditions approved unanimously.
topics.outcome: Public hearing closed and Order of Conditions approved.

topics.title: Plastic bag ban citizen petition update
topics.summary: The conservation agent reported that high school student sponsors of a proposed citizen petition banning plastic bags have withdrawn it from the upcoming Annual Town Meeting. The sponsors felt underprepared and plan to refine the proposal and reintroduce it for the fall Town Meeting.
key_details: Petition withdrawn from the Annual Town Meeting warrant.
Organizers plan to bring an updated petition to the fall Town Meeting.

topics.title: Chapter 61A Notice of Intent to Sell: Northborough Road
topics.summary: The commission discussed a Chapter 61A Notice of Intent to Sell Lot 3, an approximately 1.5-acre parcel on the south side of Northborough Road, part of the Johnson property. The conservation agent and members noted that this specific lot has limited conservation value due to its small size and proximity to already-developed frontage, while acknowledging other nearby parcels abutting the aqueduct have higher conservation significance. The commission opted not to recommend that the Select Board exercise the town's right of first refusal.
key_details: Lot 3 consists of approximately 1.5 acres on the south side of Northborough Road.
Remaining portions of the Johnson agricultural land are scheduled to exit Chapter 61A status in July.
Commissioners noted neighboring parcels near the aqueduct have far greater resource value than Lot 3.
Commission decided not to recommend exercising the town right of first refusal.
topics.outcome: No recommendation to exercise right of first refusal; no formal action taken.

topics.title: 171 Woodland Road Certificate of Compliance continuance
topics.summary: The applicant for a Certificate of Compliance at 171 Woodland Road requested a continuance because weather conditions had delayed completion of required dry well work.
key_details: DEP file number 290-1123, 171 Woodland Road.
Applicant requested continuance until dry well work is completed.

topics.title: 250 Turnpike Road 40B draft comment letter
topics.summary: The conservation agent presented a comprehensive draft comment letter intended for the Zoning Board of Appeals regarding the 250 Turnpike Road Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application. The letter highlights numerous discrepancies in recent plan revisions, including the disappearance of erosion controls from plan sheets, work limits encroaching into the local 20-foot no-touch wetland buffer, and retaining walls placed too close to property lines for practical construction. The letter also raises substantial ecological concerns about the applicant removing overhead grates from a proposed 50-plus-foot amphibian crossing tunnel, which would block essential light and moisture necessary for migration.
key_details: Comprehensive 40B housing application at 250 Turnpike Road.
Draft letter flags missing erosion control sheets, deck discrepancies, and boundary conflicts for retaining walls.
Reiterates town opposition to waivers of the 20-foot no-touch buffer zone.
Questions the effectiveness of an enclosed amphibian tunnel lacking light and moisture.
Agent is holding final submission of the letter until civil and environmental peer review reports are received the following week.
topics.outcome: Commission endorsed the draft comments; submission to the ZBA held pending peer review reports.
topics.why_it_matters: The town's feedback on this major 40B development protects local wetlands, vernal pool habitats, and private abutters from excessive stormwater and construction impacts.

topics.title: Conservation land use regulations update
topics.summary: The conservation agent reported on revisions to proposed conservation land use regulations, incorporating minor feedback from the Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee. The regulations will give the commission enforcement authority over violations and encroachments, such as unauthorized mowing on town conservation land. A formal public hearing will be scheduled for the next meeting to adopt the rules under the Conservation Commission Act.
key_details: Regulations aim to deter encroachment and unauthorized mowing on town conservation land.
Feedback integrated from the Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee.
Formal public hearing to adopt the regulations scheduled for the next commission meeting.
topics.outcome: Draft regulations to be posted for a public hearing at the next meeting.

topics.title: Conservation agent report and site updates
topics.summary: The agent provided updates on ongoing projects across town, including sinkhole repairs on Central Street and the extensive use of timber swamp mats along the reservoir by National Grid for utility work. She also noted an upcoming meeting with the owners of 241-245 Turnpike Road regarding disturbed areas and unauthorized vehicle storage, as well as required erosion control maintenance and tree replanting follow-up at the Valvoline site on Flagg Road.
key_details: Central Street sinkhole repairs are currently underway.
National Grid utility work along the reservoir is utilizing thousands of swamp mats, with work expected to conclude by fall.
Meeting scheduled next week with owners of 241-245 Turnpike Road regarding Carnova vehicle parking near a stream.
Valvoline project on Flagg Road needs sediment control maintenance and will present a tree replanting proposal after a planned hydrant relocation.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; agent will follow up on site compliance.
